people.moses.meaning: He speaks to Israel in Moab before they cross the Jordan. He tells their past again and teaches the law. He writes the law, lays his hands on Joshua, and blesses the tribes. He sees the land from Mount Nebo and dies in Moab.
people.aaron.meaning: Moses recalls the calf at Horeb. The LORD was angry enough to destroy Aaron, and Moses prayed for him. Aaron later died, and his son Eleazar became priest. The LORD tells Moses he will die as Aaron did.
people.miriam.meaning: Moses gives a rule about leprosy. Then he says, “Remember what the LORD your God did to Miriam.” He does not tell her story here.
people.joshua.role: Son of Nun who will lead after Moses
people.joshua.relations: Son of Nun. Moses lays his hands on him.
people.joshua.meaning: The LORD says Joshua will go into the land and tells Moses to encourage him. Moses tells him before all Israel to be strong. Moses lays his hands on him. After Moses dies, Israel listens to Joshua.
people.caleb.role: Son of Jephunneh who will see the land
people.caleb.relations: Son of Jephunneh. The LORD names him just before Joshua the son of Nun.
people.caleb.meaning: Moses recalls the LORD’s oath after the people refused to go up. No man of that generation will see the land except Caleb. The LORD promises him the land he walked on, because he followed the LORD.
people.dathan.role: Son of Eliab swallowed by the earth
people.dathan.relations: Son of Eliab, from Reuben’s family. Brother of Abiram.
people.dathan.meaning: Moses reminds Israel what the LORD did to Dathan and Abiram. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them. Moses says Israel saw the LORD’s work with their own eyes.
people.abiram.role: Son of Eliab swallowed by the earth
people.abiram.relations: Son of Eliab, from Reuben’s family. Brother of Dathan.
people.abiram.meaning: Moses names Abiram with his brother Dathan. The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them both. Their households, tents, and followers went down with them.
people.balaam.relations: Son of Beor, from Pethor of Mesopotamia. Balak hires him in Numbers 22.
people.balaam.meaning: A law keeps Ammonites and Moabites out of the LORD’s assembly. One reason is that they hired Balaam to curse Israel. The LORD would not listen to Balaam. He turned the curse into a blessing.
people.sihon.relations: He fights Moses and Israel. Og is the other Amorite king east of the Jordan.
people.sihon.meaning: Moses sends him words of peace and asks to pass through. Sihon refuses and comes out to fight at Jahaz. Israel takes all his cities. Moses gives that land to the Reubenites and the Gadites.
people.og.relations: He fights Moses and Israel. Sihon is the other Amorite king east of the Jordan.
people.og.meaning: Og comes out to fight Israel at Edrei. Israel defeats him and takes his sixty cities. Moses notes his iron bed, nine cubits long. Moses gives Bashan to the half-tribe of Manasseh.
people.abraham.role: First father to whom God swore the land
people.abraham.meaning: The LORD swore to give the land to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Moses repeats this oath as Israel gets ready to enter. He also prays by their names when the LORD is angry (9:27). The LORD repeats the oath to Moses on Mount Nebo.
people.lot.meaning: The LORD gave Ar to the children of Lot, who are Moab. He also gave the children of Ammon their land. So Israel must not fight them or take their land.
people.isaac.meaning: Isaac never acts alone in this book. Moses names him with Abraham and Jacob each time. The LORD swore the land to all three.
people.esau.meaning: Esau’s children live in Seir, and Moses calls them Israel’s brothers. The LORD gave Mount Seir to Esau. Israel must not fight them and must pay for food and water.
people.jacob.meaning: Moses names Jacob with Abraham and Isaac in the oath about the land. The poems in chapters 32–33 also call the people Jacob.
people.joseph.role: Son of Jacob whose tribes carry his name
people.joseph.meaning: Joseph’s tribe stands on Mount Gerizim to bless the people (chapter 27). Moses blesses Joseph’s land with dew, fruit, and the best of the hills. He says Joseph’s horns are like a wild ox’s. The horns are Ephraim and Manasseh.
people.judah.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.judah.meaning: Judah’s tribe stands on Mount Gerizim to bless the people (chapter 27). Moses asks the LORD to hear Judah’s voice. He asks the LORD to help Judah against his enemies.
people.reuben.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.reuben.meaning: Moses gives the Reubenites land east of the Jordan, taken from Sihon (chapter 3). The tribe stands on Mount Ebal for the curse (chapter 27). Moses prays, “Let Reuben live, and not die.”
people.simeon.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.simeon.meaning: Simeon’s tribe stands on Mount Gerizim to bless the people. Moses does not name Simeon in the blessings of chapter 33.
people.levi.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.levi.meaning: The LORD sets Levi’s tribe apart to carry the ark and serve him (chapter 10). Levi gets no land share, for the LORD is his share. The tribe stands on Mount Gerizim (chapter 27). Moses says they will teach Israel the law and offer sacrifices.
people.benjamin.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.benjamin.meaning: Benjamin’s tribe stands on Mount Gerizim to bless the people (chapter 27). Moses calls Benjamin the beloved of the LORD. He says Benjamin will live in safety.
people.ephraim.role: Son of Joseph whose tribe carries his name
people.ephraim.meaning: Moses names Ephraim once, inside Joseph’s blessing. He says Joseph’s horns are “the ten thousands of Ephraim.” Ephraim gets no blessing of his own.
people.manasseh.role: Son of Joseph whose tribe carries his name
people.manasseh.meaning: Moses gives the half-tribe of Manasseh the rest of Gilead and all Bashan. Jair the son of Manasseh takes the region of Argob. Joseph’s blessing ends with “the thousands of Manasseh.”
people.zebulun.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.zebulun.meaning: Zebulun’s tribe stands on Mount Ebal for the curse (chapter 27). Moses tells Zebulun to rejoice in his going out. He says Zebulun and Issachar will call peoples to the mountain to offer sacrifices.
people.issachar.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.issachar.meaning: Issachar’s tribe stands on Mount Gerizim to bless the people (chapter 27). Moses tells Issachar to rejoice in his tents. Issachar shares this blessing with Zebulun.
people.dan.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.dan.meaning: Dan’s tribe stands on Mount Ebal for the curse (chapter 27). Moses calls Dan a lion’s cub that leaps out of Bashan.
people.naphtali.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.naphtali.meaning: Naphtali’s tribe stands on Mount Ebal for the curse (chapter 27). Moses says Naphtali is full of the LORD’s blessing. He tells the tribe to possess the west and the south.
people.gad.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.gad.meaning: Moses gives the Gadites land east of the Jordan with the Reubenites (chapter 3). The tribe stands on Mount Ebal for the curse (chapter 27). Moses says Gad lives like a lioness and took the first part for himself.
people.asher.role: Son of Jacob whose tribe carries his name
people.asher.meaning: Asher’s tribe stands on Mount Ebal for the curse (chapter 27). Moses says Asher is blessed with children. He asks that Asher dip his foot in oil and stay strong all his days.
places.egypt.summary: Moses reminds Israel that they were slaves in Egypt. The LORD brought them out (chapter 5). Chapter 11 says Egypt’s fields were watered by foot. Chapter 28 warns of the diseases of Egypt.
places.egypt.limits: The marker shows the Nile valley as a whole region.
places.sinai.summary: Deuteronomy mostly calls this mountain Horeb. There the LORD spoke from the fire and made a covenant (chapters 4–5). Israel made the calf there, and Moses broke the tablets (chapter 9).
places.sinai.limits: People disagree about which mountain this is. The marker shows a traditional region.
places.kadesh.summary: The scouts return to Kadesh Barnea with fruit and a good report (chapter 1). The people still refuse to go up. They stay there many days.
places.kadesh.limits: The marker shows the traditional Ain el-Qudeirat region. The camp’s exact place is not known.
places.canaan.summary: Moses prepares Israel to cross the Jordan into this land. The LORD swore it to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (chapter 1). Moses sees it from Mount Nebo but does not enter (chapter 34).
places.canaan.limits: The marker shows a wide region, not an exact border.
places.hebron.summary: Deuteronomy does not name Hebron. The scouts reach Hebron in Numbers 13.
places.hebron.limits: The modern city shows the general location.
places.edom.summary: Esau’s children live in Seir. The LORD tells Israel not to fight them (chapter 2). Chapter 23 calls an Edomite Israel’s brother.
places.edom.limits: The marker shows a wide region, not an exact border.
places.moab.summary: Moses speaks this whole book in the land of Moab, beyond the Jordan (chapter 1). He dies there, and Israel weeps for him thirty days (chapter 34).
places.moab.limits: The marker shows the general region. The camp’s exact place is not known.
places.heshbon.summary: Sihon king of the Amorites lives at Heshbon. He refuses to let Israel pass, and Israel takes his cities (chapter 2).
places.heshbon.limits: Tall Hisban is the traditional site. Its remains alone do not prove Sihon’s rule.
places.bashan.summary: Og king of Bashan fights Israel at Edrei and loses (chapter 3). Moses gives Bashan to the half-tribe of Manasseh. He sets apart Golan in Bashan for a manslayer to flee to (chapter 4).
places.bashan.limits: The marker shows a wide region, not one town.
places.gilead.summary: Israel takes all Gilead (chapter 3). Moses gives half its hill country to the Reubenites and Gadites. He gives the rest to the half-tribe of Manasseh. He sets apart Ramoth in Gilead for a manslayer to flee to (chapter 4).
places.gilead.limits: The marker shows a wide region, not an exact border.
places.nebo.summary: The LORD tells Moses to climb Mount Nebo and see Canaan (chapter 32). Moses goes up, sees the land, and dies in Moab (chapter 34).
places.nebo.limits: The marker shows the traditional Nebo location. No one knows where Moses’s tomb is (34:6).
places.gerizim.summary: Moses says to set the blessing on Mount Gerizim (chapter 11). Six tribes will stand there to bless the people (chapter 27).
places.gerizim.limits: The marker shows the mountain. Deuteronomy plans this event but does not show it happen.
places.ebal.summary: Moses says to set the curse on Mount Ebal (chapter 11). Israel must set up plastered stones and an altar there (chapter 27). Six tribes will stand there for the curse.
places.ebal.limits: The marker shows the mountain. It does not date the altar or show its exact place.
sources.web.limits: The stories, speeches, and laws are evidence from the text. They do not prove each event on their own.
sources.terrain.limits: Modern terrain is a map aid. It does not show ancient shorelines or settlements.
sources.atlas-exodus.limits: The route shown is a study tradition. It does not prove a sea crossing or a Sinai site.
sources.yale-11.summary: Hayes studies the book’s speeches, adapted laws, and central worship. She also covers care for outsiders and the change of leaders.
sources.yale-11.limits: This is one university lecture’s reading. Scholars debate the proposed stages and dates of writing. They do not set the historical dates of Moses’s speeches.
sources.lds-prophet.limits: This Restoration scripture gives a later reading or comparison. It is separate from Deuteronomy’s own words.
sources.lds-agency.limits: This Restoration scripture gives a later reading or comparison. It is separate from Deuteronomy’s own words.
sources.lds-moses.limits: This Restoration scripture gives a later reading or comparison. It is separate from Deuteronomy’s own words.
sources.net-deut-32.limits: These are scholarly translation notes. Their choice of an original reading is an editors’ judgment. This guide did not review all the manuscripts.
sources.dm-deuteronomy.limits: This is an older scholarly reading, separate from Church teaching. The proposed order of events was not checked here. Hebrew and Greek text is not copied from the post.
chapters.*.mapNote: Moses speaks in Moab, and the other points show places he names. Regions and traditional sites are approximate.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The line shows the trip from Horeb to Kadesh that Moses recalls in chapter 1. It is a simple line, and the camps along it are not known.
sources.scholar-weinfeld.limits: The publisher description and edition metadata were reviewed. The full commentary was not read. This record verifies identity and scope. It does not independently verify every argument.
